title: Citigroup and Axis Bank Partner to Finance NRI Foreign-Currency Deposits
excerpt: The cross-border arrangement allows NRIs to leverage FCNR deposits as the RBI's concessional scheme attracts over $65 billion in just 11 weeks.
body:
• Citigroup has partnered with Axis Bank to finance NRIs investing in foreign-currency deposits in India, with Axis Bank issuing standby letters of credit to support Citigroup's offshore financing
  • The RBI's concessional FCNR deposit scheme has attracted $65.4 billion in 11 weeks, prompting the central bank to close the window ahead of schedule
  • Axis Bank is offering interest rates up to 6.40% on FCNR deposits and expects its market share in foreign deposit flows to exceed its organic share
  • The partnership does not mark Citigroup's return to India's consumer banking market, which it sold to Axis Bank in 2022

Citigroup has partnered with Axis Bank to finance non-resident Indians investing in foreign-currency deposits in India, creating a cross-border channel that could increase dollar inflows from the diaspora, according to The American Bazaar and Mint.

Under the arrangement, Axis Bank will issue standby letters of credit to support financing provided by Citigroup through its offshore operations. The structure allows NRIs to leverage money invested in FCNR (Foreign Currency Non-Resident) deposits, potentially multiplying the funds flowing into India's banking system.

RBI's Deposit Push

The partnership rides on the Reserve Bank of India's aggressive push to attract foreign currency. The central bank introduced a concessional swap facility in June to encourage banks to mobilize FCNR deposits, and later clarified that Indian banks can extend loans to non-residents or issue guarantees in favor of foreign lenders against such deposits.

The response has been substantial. Deposits mobilized under the RBI facility reached $65.4 billion as of August 13, according to RBI data cited by Mint. The strong inflows prompted the central bank to pull the facility's closing date forward to the end of August from September 30.

"The first thing banks will do is reduce or pause growth in other very expensive deposits for some time."

— Amitabh Chaudhry, CEO, Axis Bank

What It Means for NRI Investors

For NRIs, the arrangement offers another way to earn returns on dollar savings while keeping funds in foreign-currency deposits with an Indian bank. Axis Bank is offering interest rates up to 6.40% on FCNR deposits. The leverage structure could make larger deposits particularly attractive to wealthy diaspora investors who want to deploy capital in India without converting to rupees.

The framework has also opened a path for global banks with offshore private-banking networks to participate in the Indian deposit market without maintaining a retail presence in the country. Individual banks determine the level of financing they are prepared to provide.

Banks Eye Cheaper Funding

Indian banks have been grappling with a funding squeeze as loan growth outpaces deposit growth. Loans expanded 18% in the two weeks ended May 31, the fastest pace in nearly two years, while deposits grew just 12% over the same period, according to RBI data. Some lenders resorted to certificates of deposit with rates as high as 7.53% for three-month paper.

Axis Bank CEO Amitabh Chaudhry told Bloomberg News that banks will likely use the new foreign-currency deposits to replace expensive funding on their balance sheets before channeling the money to companies. He identified infrastructure projects, data-center investments, commercial real estate, and large capital-expenditure plans as the quickest areas for deployment.

Axis Bank expects its share of FCNR deposit flows to exceed its organic market share of 5.1%, CFO Puneet Sharma said during the bank's June quarter earnings call.

Not a Consumer Banking Return

The deal does not signal Citigroup's return to India's consumer banking market. The company sold its Indian consumer banking operations to Axis Bank in 2022 and continues to focus on institutional clients in the country. This is a wholesale financing arrangement that leverages Citigroup's offshore network and Axis Bank's domestic deposit franchise.

The last time the RBI ran a similar scheme during the taper tantrum in 2013, the banking industry raised about $34 billion from FCNR deposits. HDFC Bank led the mobilization with $3.4 billion, followed by SBI at $3.07 billion and ICICI Bank at $2 billion, according to a Macquarie Capital Securities note. The current scheme has already nearly doubled that figure.
nri_angle: The partnership gives NRIs a new way to earn returns on dollar savings through leveraged FCNR deposits with Axis Bank, backed by Citigroup's offshore financing.
author: Diaspora Desk
